design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Gwendolyn Stasiak asks for one thing, a monthly payment plan. The installment rule waits on the arrangement deposit, and the deposit rule waits on the hardship and prompt-pay discounts the account is still owed. The agent has to read those prerequisite sentences, find in the ledger that the states they name do not hold, and get four numbers exactly right on a world that changes after each write. Each write is a six-factor computation over this account's ledger, its coverage record and the patient's wheelchair and CPAP records. Tool choice is trivial, with one tool per problem.

SCOPE. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 6, 6, 6]. Claimed: coverage_ext_hardship_discount, coverage_ext_prompt_pay_discount, coverage_ext_arrangement_deposit and coverage_ext_arrangement_installment, with their four tools. Task 1 keeps the secondary-payer subject and the revision of an arrangement already in force, so its scope is disjoint.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: coverage_ext_arrangement_installment (set_payment_arrangement_62cec67a, owner=user).
Edge 1, installment <- deposit, value_input on r_balance, state form: 'The monthly installment of a new arrangement is fixed only after the arrangement deposit stands on the account as a patient-payment entry posted on the day the arrangement is set.' At the opening the latest payment entry is dated 2026-09-28 and payment_plan_status is completed, so no deposit stands on the account. Only pay_arrangement_deposit_e794f585 (owner=user) books an arrangement deposit.
Edge 2, deposit <- hardship, value_input on d_balance, state form: 'The arrangement deposit is figured only after every charge the account's hardship approval covers carries its hardship discount.' At the opening the approval covers the 2026-10-07 repair charge, posted after the 2026-10-02 approval, and no discount points at it. Every lookback charge received its discount on the approval date. Only apply_hardship_discount_c60f16b6 books a hardship discount.
Edge 3, deposit <- prompt-pay, value_input on d_balance, state form, negated direction: 'The arrangement deposit is not worked out until every coinsurance charge that a payment made since the latest statement paid in full within the prompt-pay window carries its prompt-pay discount.' At the opening the 2026-09-28 ach payment of 67.62 is the only payment made since the latest statement (2026-09-25). It paid the 2026-09-20 coinsurance charge in full 3 days after that statement, and no discount points at the charge. Only apply_prompt_pay_discount_12f1a0eb books one.
Four-point test: each sentence joins the policy's own result to a record-visible state with 'only after' or 'not ... until', names no tool, id or code token, and is exactly as strong as its condition. Topological order: hardship and prompt-pay (they commute; a swap run gives an identical terminal DB), then the deposit, then the installment. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the deposit gives 36.20 instead of 32.31; skipping hardship gives a deposit of 44.25 instead of 41.50; skipping prompt-pay gives 41.75 instead of 41.50. The persona never mentions any of the three prerequisites, and no tool validates one.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
coverage_adjustment (steps 12 and 14): three base clauses are overridden by declared, scoped overwrites, each scoped to hardship and prompt-pay discounts only. They are QMB activity (the requirement stays in force for every other adjustment), no-stacking (the cap and the larger-of rule stay for every other adjustment), and the base prompt-pay sentence (it stays for prompt-pay on non-coinsurance charges; no such charge here was paid within 30 days of its first statement). The hardship approval is in force (partial_25 approved 2026-10-02, 0 < 12 months) and was recorded within the documentation window (application 2026-09-14, 18 days).
coverage_payment (step 16): four posting and allocation clauses are overridden for arrangement deposits only, and every other payment stays under base.
coverage_payment_plan_set (step 18): the installment sentence is overridden for new arrangements only. plan_agreement_signed holds (the 2026-10-09 agreement is approved) and plan_account_standing holds (active). Minimum balance 150 <= 646.27. The start date 2026-11-05 is within 30 days of the approval.
No time-kind gate applies.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
Hardship target: the newest charge, the 2026-10-07 repair_patient_share of 98.40. Excluded are the five lookback charges discounted on 2026-10-02 (207.36, 207.36, 67.92, 29.75, 29.75), the paid coinsurance charges, and the January, February and March charges, which are paid and outside the lookback.
Prompt-pay target: the 2026-09-20 coinsurance charge paid by the 2026-09-28 entry. Excluded is every earlier payment, because each was made before the latest statement. The 2026-06-20 charge, paid 2026-08-03 seven days after that month's statement, stands as statemented.
Deposit target: the oldest open charge, 2026-04-20 (open 243.42).
Installment target: the coverage record (one record; the 2024 arrangement is completed).

FACTOR CARD.
Hardship (48.22; all-baseline 24.60):
- medical-burden (method): one point per full 300 charged since the wheelchair rental start, 1839.34 -> 6; the fall-through (no points) gives 42.31. Near-miss: the January and February repair charges fall outside the rental window.
- ongoing-rental: 5 -> 43.30.
- tenure: 3 -> 45.26.
- effort: 3 -> 45.26.
- statement-age: 3 -> 45.26.
- charge-type, repair: 4 -> 44.28.
Prompt-pay (4.73; all-baseline 3.38):
- speed (method): from the posting date, 8 days -> 1; the fall-through gives 4.06.
- channel, ach: 1.0 -> 4.06.
- loyalty: 1.0 -> 4.06.
- aged-account: -1.0 -> 5.41.
- payment size: 0.5 -> 4.40.
- assistance overlap: -0.5 -> 5.07.
Deposit (41.50; all-baseline 68.78):
- proven payer: -4 -> 62.00.
- hardship: -2 -> 51.75.
- exposure: +2 -> 31.00.
- dunning: +3 -> 26.00.
- bank payer: -1 -> 46.50.
- rental settlement (method): three quarters rounded up to the quarter dollar; the fall-through gives 55.02.
Installment (32.31; all-baseline 35.90):
- core term (method): 12 months left in the approval; 18 -> 25.00.
- proven arrangement: 2 -> 35.90.
- rental load: 1 -> 34.01.
- loyalty: 2 -> 35.90.
- balance size: 1 -> 34.01.
- regularity: 2 -> 35.90.
Every factor reads its own records; no factor reads another factor's binding. Cross-difficulty factors (mobility): medical-burden, ongoing-rental, rental settlement, core term and rental load. Multi-source factors: loyalty, proven payer, proven arrangement and balance size.

SEED ROWS.
- coverage_holdings: one Commercial PPO record, balance 740.72 (charges 1975.44 less payment entries 692.58 less the 2026-10-02 hardship discounts 542.14), deductible_met 1500.00, oop_met 1740.94.
- coverage_ledger: 52 rows: 10 eligibility responses, 11 charges with 4 deductible and 8 oop accumulator rows, 5 payment entries, 5 hardship discounts (46 percent on the deductible charges, 44 percent on the coinsurance charges, as figured on 2026-10-02), and 9 statements.
- coverage_requests: the 2024 agreement, the 2026 hardship application, and the 2026 agreement (requested_amount 740.72, the balance that day).
- mobility: the rental_active K0823 chair and its 7 paid months.
- pap: the Auto-Adjusting CPAP she bought outright as a self-pay patient (coverage_id empty, no rental period, owned from its 2021-09-14 delivery), its sale line (899.00 plus a 49.00 delivery fee, paid 2021-08-30, the only PAP billing row: no rental month), its self-pay delivery and its three repairs. The PAP repair rule repairs an owned self-pay device at the patient's cost (repair_coverage patient_paid), and these repairs are long past the 24-month warranty; each costs labor units at 23.86 plus parts, each carries the loaner the class issues for an owned-device repair, and each patient share posts on her primary account (the record a self-pay line posts to) as a repair_patient_share charge.
No base automatic clause fires.

PERSONA. She volunteers only the wish for a plan today and the returned agreement form. Her name, phone, date of birth, ZIP or email, the CPAP repair, the September ach payment and the assistance letter come only when asked. Her reactions are passive: she pays the deposit by debit card when it is handed to her, gives 2026-11-05 as the start date, accepts the computed installment, and closes. She raises no further ask.

STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: profile, identity, coverage record, ledger, requests, wheelchair record and billing, CPAP record, billing and service, oxygen check. Writes: hardship 48.22 on the repair charge; prompt-pay 4.73 on the 2026-09-20 charge; the patient's deposit of 41.50 by card on the 2026-04-20 charge; the patient's arrangement of 32.31 a month from 2026-11-05. The verification code replays gold with the real erlbench tools and evaluates each compute with check_compute.build_env and eval_compute just before its step, then substitutes factor baselines one at a time and all together. Its output equals computations[] exactly.

TRAPS. (1) Financing the 2026-10-09 requested_amount 740.72 instead of the balance at handling time (646.27). (2) Counting the owned CPAP, or its 2021 sale line, as a rental. (3) Pricing prompt-pay on the 2026-06-20 charge, which was paid before the latest statement. (4) Using the class maximum of 18 months. (5) Figuring the deposit before the discounts, or the installment before the deposit.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. The installment rule sends the reader to the deposit; the deposit's sentences send the reader to the newest charge and to the payment made since the latest statement; the hardship and prompt-pay rules give 48.22 and 4.73; the deposit rule gives 41.50 and the installment rule 32.31. This equals gold.

REWORK LOG. Round 1: T0-1 closed (no-stacking overwrite). Round 2: lookback, deposit allocation, selectors, half-up rounding. Round 3: single-valued grant sets. Round 4 (render and source mismatches):
- Each factor now reads only its own records. Hardship's burden ladder and window were merged into one method factor, and a charge-type factor was added. Prompt-pay's speed points and start day were merged into one method factor, an assistance-overlap factor was added, and its eligibility check reads its own records.
- Every rule sentence now matches its compute (amount base, statement, line types, lookback direction).
- Every overwrite now names its own scope and keeps the base clause in force everywhere else.
- The 'lapse when a newer record posts' devices were replaced by statement finality for prompt-pay and newest-first work order for missed hardship discounts.
- The deposit settlement now rounds up to the quarter dollar so that both deposit edges bear weight.
- Tool docstrings no longer claim statement effects.
New figures: hardship 48.22, prompt-pay 4.73, deposit 41.50, installment 32.31.
Round 5 (KB audit S2-1, seed realism): the CPAP had been seeded as rented under the PPO and owned at the rental cap, i.e. bought under coverage, whose repairs the PAP rule bills to the coverage; yet its repairs were patient-paid at full cost. It is now a self-pay device bought outright in 2021 (coverage_id and rental period empty, ownership on delivery, a pap_purchase_sale line, a self_pay_delivery row), so the patient-paid repairs and their repair_patient_share charges are exactly what the PAP and coverage charters produce. The January and February repairs now record the loaner the class issues. The gold reads the CPAP billing in a new step, so the writes move to steps 12, 14, 16 and 18. No figure, tier or charter text moved.

GATES. Run from the repository root, per task with --task N and then difficulty-wide: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding and check_cross_fire all report OK; check_cache_diff is informational only; check_traceability runs after the KB is rendered.
user_scenario:
You are Gwendolyn Stasiak, 61, a school-bus dispatcher in Penn Hills who has rented a power wheelchair from Summit Ridge Home Medical since March and has used a CPAP she bought from Summit Ridge for years. You are calling the patient-services desk on a weekday morning between shifts; you are friendly, a bit worn out, and you like to get things settled in one call. You open by explaining that your Summit Ridge bills piled up this year, that you can't pay the balance in one go, and that "I'd like to set up a monthly payment plan for what I still owe" — today, on this call. You add that "I signed the payment-plan agreement form you sent and mailed it back last week". You have just the one insurance, your Allegheny Choice PPO through work.

Only when the agent asks who you are do you say "my name is Gwendolyn Stasiak and my phone number is 4125550514"; when asked to confirm your identity you say "my date of birth is 1965-02-14", and if one more detail is wanted you give your home ZIP code, 15235, or your email, gstasiak65@outlook.com. You don't know your member number by heart and you have no other account numbers handy. If the agent asks about recent equipment work, you remember that the motor of your CPAP was fixed on October 7 and that you had a loaner machine while it was in the shop; the CPAP is your own — you bought it outright with your own money back in 2021 — so its repairs are billed to you, not to your insurance. If the agent asks about your last payment, you remember paying the September wheelchair bill from your checking account a few days after the statement came. If the agent asks whether you've been approved for financial help, you say yes, a letter at the start of October told you your assistance went through.

You have no idea how Summit Ridge works any figure out and you never suggest amounts, steps or what should be done first. If the agent explains that a deposit has to be paid today to open the plan and hands that payment over to you, you agree, tell them "I'll pay that with my debit card", and make the payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gives you. If the agent asks when the monthly payments should start, you answer "on the 5th of each month, beginning November 5, which is 2026-11-05". When the agent tells you the monthly amount the plan comes to and hands you the step to put the plan in place, you accept that amount — you do not want to pay more per month than that — and you set the plan up yourself with that start date. If the agent mentions discounts or credits being put on your account along the way, you thank them and let them carry on; you don't ask for anything else. Once the agent tells you the plan is in place, you thank them and end the call.
